lessons.title: Unit 10 Consolidation: caudillos and personal power
lessons.goal: Review the caudillo, personal power, the montoneras, the debate over order and the legacy of caudillismo.

lessons.title: What is a nation?
lessons.goal: Read about the difference between a state and a nation, and use relative clauses with a preposition to describe the country and the community people belonged to.

lessons.title: National symbols: flags, anthems and heroes
lessons.goal: Read how flags, anthems and statues were made in the new republics, and use the passive with se to say what was created and when.

lessons.title: Creating an identity: the eagle and the serpent
lessons.goal: Read how new countries used the past to build an identity, and use the subjunctive after value judgments to say what is important or necessary.

lessons.title: Peoples and borders: the Paraguayan War and the War of the Pacific
lessons.goal: Read how two wars changed borders and how borders cut through communities, and use aunque to hold an official claim and a messier reality together.

lessons.title: Imagining the nation: schools, history books and novels
lessons.goal: Read how schools, books and novels helped to imagine the nation, and use the passive with ser to say who presented what.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 11 Consolidation: nation and nationalism
lessons.goal: Review how the new republics tried to build a nation: ideas, symbols, borders and schools.

lessons.title: Liberal ideas: freedom, equality and who could vote
lessons.grammar: Cuanto más… más and a medida que
lessons.goal: Read about the ideas of 19th-century liberals and who was left out, and use proportional constructions to say how one change led to another.

lessons.title: Reforming the state: the Reforma in Mexico
lessons.goal: Read how Mexican liberals changed the law, the land and the constitution, and use the passive with ser to say what was approved and who was elected.

lessons.title: Church and State: three paths
lessons.goal: Read how Mexico, Ecuador and Colombia treated the power of the Church, and use impersonal se to say what was decided and what was possible.

lessons.title: Modernizing society: railways, ports and immigrants
lessons.goal: Read how railways, ports and immigration changed Latin America in the late 19th century, and use the gerund to say what happened at the same time.

lessons.title: A new model: order, progress and exports
lessons.goal: Read how positivism and the export economy shaped the liberal period, and use ordering markers to weigh its gains and its limits.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 12 Consolidation: liberalism and modernization
lessons.goal: Review liberal ideas, the Mexican Reforma, Church and State, railways and immigrants, and the export model.

lessons.title: The export model: selling to the world
lessons.goal: Say what Latin American countries sold abroad between 1870 and 1914 and who paid for it, using relative clauses.

lessons.title: Products and raw materials: coffee, meat, saltpetre and bananas
lessons.goal: Say what each region exported, using cuyo, cuya, cuyos and cuyas.

lessons.title: Railways, ports and markets: an economy built to export
lessons.goal: Describe how railways and ports served exports, using aunque.

lessons.title: Work, land and inequality in the export boom
lessons.goal: Describe who owned the land and who did the work, using the pluperfect.

lessons.title: Dependence and vulnerability: Peru's guano and Chile's nitrates
lessons.goal: Tell how guano and saltpetre booms ended, using dejar de + infinitive.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 13 review: the export economies
lessons.grammar: unit review: relative clauses, cuyo, aunque, pluperfect, dejar de
lessons.goal: Review the export model, its products, railways, land and labour, and the guano boom.

lessons.title: New cities: trams, avenues and the outskirts
lessons.goal: Describe how Latin American cities looked and grew around 1900, using the imperfect.

lessons.title: New social classes: the middle class and the workers
lessons.grammar: reporting with según and decir que (recap)
lessons.goal: Say who the new middle class and the workers were and what they asked for, reporting what historians and workers said.

lessons.title: Immigration: how people came and where they settled
lessons.goal: Tell how immigrants travelled and settled, using a través de and por medio de.

lessons.title: Work and conflict: unions, strikes and repression
lessons.goal: Tell how unions and strikes were met with force, using the passive with ser.

lessons.title: A society in transformation: the university reform and women's rights
lessons.goal: Tell how students and women asked for change, using aunque.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 14 review: cities, classes, immigrants, strikes and reform
lessons.grammar: unit review: imperfect, según, a través de, passive with ser, aunque
lessons.goal: Review the social changes in Latin America between 1870 and 1930.

lessons.title: What is a revolution?
lessons.goal: Say what a revolution is and how it differs from a coup, using relative clauses.

lessons.title: Land and power: why land mattered
lessons.goal: Explain why land and power were linked, using debido a and a raíz de.

lessons.title: Workers and social movements
lessons.goal: Say who made up the social movements and how they acted, using the gerund.

lessons.title: Revolution and the State: what the new governments had to do
lessons.goal: Say what new governments had to do and what others thought they should do, using tener que and deber.

lessons.title: When the order changes: why revolutions happen
lessons.grammar: opinions with creer que and no creer que (recap)
lessons.goal: Say what historians think about the causes of revolutions, using creer que and no creer que.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 15 review: revolutions in Latin America
lessons.grammar: unit review: relative clauses, debido a, gerund, tener que, creer que
lessons.goal: Review what revolutions are, why they happen and what new governments faced.

lessons.title: The Porfiriato: Díaz, progress and land
lessons.goal: Say how long something had been going on, with *llevar* + gerund, to describe Mexico before 1910.

lessons.title: Madero and the fall of Díaz
lessons.goal: Report what Díaz and Madero said, with reported speech in the past.

lessons.title: Zapata and Villa: two leaders, two armies
lessons.goal: Tell the story of Zapata and Villa with the preterite and the imperfect.

lessons.title: The Constitution of 1917: land, work and school
lessons.goal: Describe the Constitution of 1917 with relative clauses that take a preposition.

lessons.title: The legacy of the Revolution: one party and land reform
lessons.goal: Say what was done after the Revolution, with the passive with *ser*.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 16 Consolidation: the Mexican Revolution
lessons.goal: Review the Mexican Revolution, from Díaz to Cárdenas, with the grammar of Unit 16.

lessons.title: Stronger states, 1900-1930
lessons.goal: Say what the new states created, with the passive with *se*.

lessons.title: Cultural nationalism: murals, indigenismo and modernism
lessons.goal: Describe the cultural movements of the 1920s with *a pesar de*, *a pesar de que* and *pese a*.

lessons.title: Education and the nation: the rural school
lessons.goal: Describe changes that grow together, with *a medida que* and *cuanto más ..., más ...*.

lessons.title: Populations and territories: the State reaches further
lessons.goal: Describe how people lived and travelled, with impersonal *se*.

lessons.title: The modern State
lessons.goal: Say how the State changed, with verbs of change.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 17 Consolidation: nationalism and the State
lessons.goal: Review the stronger states of 1900-1930, with the grammar of Unit 17.

lessons.title: The crisis of 1929
lessons.goal: Say what had already happened before the crash of 1929, with the pluperfect.

lessons.title: Latin America and the crisis
lessons.goal: Show a contrast, with *sin embargo* and *no obstante*, to explain how the crisis hit Latin America.

lessons.title: Less trade, less income
lessons.goal: Say how serious the crisis was, with superlatives such as *la peor crisis*.

lessons.title: Changing the economic model
lessons.goal: Say by what means governments changed the economy, with *mediante*.

lessons.title: A crisis that transformed the region
lessons.goal: Sum up the changes of the 1930s, with argument markers such as *por un lado ... por otro lado* and *en resumen*.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 18 Consolidation: the Great Depression
lessons.goal: Review the crisis of 1929 and its effects on Latin America, with the grammar of Unit 18.

lessons.title: What is populism?
lessons.goal: Learn how Latin American populism is usually defined, what features historians point to, and why the word is disputed.

lessons.title: Perón and Argentina
lessons.goal: Follow Perón's rise and fall in Argentina, telling the story with the preterite and the imperfect.

lessons.title: Cárdenas in Mexico and Vargas in Brazil
lessons.grammar: Possessive relative: cuyo, cuya, cuyos, cuyas
lessons.goal: Compare two presidents, Lázaro Cárdenas in Mexico and Getúlio Vargas in Brazil, using cuyo to link a leader to his government and laws.

lessons.title: The people and the leader
lessons.grammar: Opinion verbs and mood: creer que, no creer que
lessons.goal: Look at the link between the leader and the people, and say who believes what, using creer que and no creer que.

lessons.title: The populist legacy
lessons.grammar: Contrast connectors: sin embargo, no obstante, aunque
lessons.goal: Weigh the legacy of populist governments, with results that people praise and results that people criticise, using contrast connectors.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 19 Consolidation: Populism
lessons.goal: Review the unit on populism: the definition, Perón, Cárdenas and Vargas, the people and the leader, and the legacy.

lessons.title: Making things at home: import substitution
lessons.grammar: Cause connectors: debido a, a raíz de
lessons.goal: Learn why Latin American countries began to make at home what they had imported, and how CEPAL and tariffs fit in, using debido a and a raíz de.

lessons.title: New industries: steel, oil and cars
lessons.goal: See how governments and foreign companies built new industries in Latin America, and say how it was done with mediante.

lessons.title: Migration from the countryside to the cities
lessons.goal: Follow the millions of people who left the countryside for the cities, and say what they stopped doing and what they kept doing with dejar de.

lessons.title: The new urban societies
lessons.grammar: Verbs of change: convertirse en, hacerse, volverse
lessons.goal: Look at the new neighbourhoods, workers and middle classes of the cities, and say how they changed with verbs of change.

lessons.title: An industrial continent
lessons.grammar: Concession: a pesar de, a pesar de que
lessons.goal: Weigh what industrialisation achieved by the 1960s against its limits, using a pesar de.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 20 Consolidation: Industrialization
lessons.goal: Review the unit on industrialization: import substitution, new industries, migration, new urban societies and the balance of results and limits.

lessons.title: Cuba before 1959
lessons.goal: See what Cuba was like before the revolution, and describe how things used to be with soler.

lessons.title: Fidel Castro and the revolution
lessons.goal: Follow the rebels from the Moncada attack to the fall of Batista, and say what had already happened with the pluperfect.

lessons.title: A socialist revolution
lessons.goal: Follow the radical steps of the revolution, the break with the United States and the debate about its results, using cuanto más… más…

lessons.title: The Bay of Pigs and the missile crisis
lessons.goal: Follow the invasion of 1961 and the missile crisis of 1962, and say what was about to happen with estar a punto de.

lessons.title: Cuba and Latin America
lessons.goal: See how the revolution reached the rest of Latin America, and say what was done to Cuba and to Che Guevara with the ser passive.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 21 Consolidation: The Cuban Revolution
lessons.goal: Review the unit on the Cuban revolution: Cuba before 1959, the rebels, the socialist turn, the Bay of Pigs and the missile crisis, and Cuba in Latin America.

lessons.title: Dos bloques
lessons.grammar: Ya sea... ya sea: presentar dos opciones formales
lessons.goal: Read how the post-1945 world split into US-led and Soviet-led blocs, the containment doctrine, and the nuclear arms race, and why Latin America became a particularly sensitive Cold War terrain.

lessons.title: América Latina en la Guerra Fría
lessons.grammar: Con tal de que + subjuntivo: una condición explícita
lessons.goal: Read how Kennedy's Alliance for Progress offered aid conditioned on moderate reform and anti-communist alignment, and why some governments implemented real reforms.

lessons.title: Revolución o anticomunismo
lessons.grammar: No cabe duda de que: afirmar con seguridad
lessons.goal: Read how Cold War logic polarized Latin American politics, the military's National Security Doctrine and the School of the Americas, and the radicalization it triggered on the left.

lessons.title: Intervención extranjera
lessons.grammar: So pretexto de: una justificación oficial cuestionable
lessons.goal: Read how both superpowers intervened directly in Latin America -- the 1954 CIA-backed coup in Guatemala, the 1965 US intervention in the Dominican Republic, and Soviet-Cuban support for guerrillas.

lessons.title: Un continente dividido
lessons.grammar: No hay + sustantivo + que no: una afirmación universal
lessons.goal: Read a closing synthesis of how thoroughly Cold War polarization touched universities, unions and militaries across Latin America, setting up the coups and repression to come.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 22 Consolidation
lessons.goal: Consolidate Cold War, ideology, intervention and conflict.

lessons.title: El vecino del norte
lessons.grammar: Tan... como: comparar poder y tamaño
lessons.goal: Read how the Monroe Doctrine evolved from a defense of the young Latin American republics into a claimed US right to intervene, and the deep, mutual asymmetry that shaped the relationship.

lessons.title: Intervenciones
lessons.grammar: Mientras tanto: dos historias que ocurren a la vez
lessons.goal: Read how the Good Neighbor policy ended direct occupations of Haiti and Nicaragua, how Panama's 1903 independence was tied to the Panama Canal, and why US intervention never depended on a communist threat.

lessons.title: Economía y dependencia
lessons.grammar: Cuanto más... (tanto) más: relaciones que crecen juntas
lessons.goal: Read how US corporate control of key industries, single-export vulnerability, and foreign debt created economic dependency, as the 1954 Guatemala coup shows.

lessons.title: Alianza para el Progreso
lessons.grammar: A raíz de: el origen de un cambio
lessons.goal: Read how the Alliance for Progress began in March 1961 to counter the Cuban Revolution, why local elites resisted its reforms, and how US enthusiasm faded after Vietnam and the 1969 change of administration.

lessons.title: Una relación compleja
lessons.grammar: Así como: comparar y sumar elementos paralelos
lessons.goal: Read a closing synthesis of the unit: intervention and economic dependency were real, but so were migration, cultural exchange, and mutual influence.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 23 Consolidation
lessons.goal: Consolidate US regional influence, intervention, economic relations and policy responses.

lessons.title: Los golpes de Estado
lessons.grammar: Más bien: matizar en vez de simplemente contrastar
lessons.goal: Read how the 1964-1976 wave of military coups produced a distinctly institutional kind of authoritarian rule, and O'Donnell's concept of the bureaucratic-authoritarian state.

lessons.title: Brasil
lessons.grammar: De tal manera que: describir un resultado
lessons.goal: Read how Brazil's 1964 coup produced two decades of Institutional Acts and escalating censorship alongside a rapid "economic miracle", ending in a gradual return to civilian rule by 1985.

lessons.title: Chile
lessons.grammar: Tras: indicar lo que viene después
lessons.goal: Read how the 1973 coup against Allende ended in his death and Pinochet's seventeen-year rule, and how the regime's free-market "Chicago Boys" experiment outlasted the dictatorship itself.

lessons.title: Argentina
lessons.goal: Read how Argentina's 1976 coup and its "National Reorganization Process" promised order and modernization, but ended in debt, deindustrialization, and a lost war that forced the return to elections in 1983.

lessons.title: El poder militar
lessons.goal: Read a closing comparison of Brazil, Chile, and Argentina's military governments, the Operation Condor repression coordinated across the Southern Cone, and why no regime lasted indefinitely.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 24 Consolidation
lessons.goal: Consolidate coups, military governments and authoritarianism.

lessons.title: El Estado represivo
lessons.grammar: En virtud de: la base legal de una acción
lessons.goal: Read how the region's military governments dressed repression in a legal facade -- states of siege, raids by security forces, and clandestine detention centers.

lessons.title: Censura y persecución
lessons.grammar: Con el fin de: expresar un propósito
lessons.goal: Read how these regimes' quieter, everyday campaign against expression worked -- press censorship, book burning, university purges, and exile.

lessons.title: Desaparecidos
lessons.grammar: Aun cuando: una concesión más fuerte que aunque
lessons.goal: Read how enforced disappearance worked as a deliberate method, the official denial that surrounded it, and how the Mothers of Plaza de Mayo turned grief into a lasting form of resistance.

lessons.title: Resistencia
lessons.grammar: Cabe destacar que: señalar un dato importante
lessons.goal: Read how resistance to repression took many forms -- human rights organizations, Pérez Esquivel's 1980 Nobel Peace Prize, international solidarity, and a smaller armed resistance.

lessons.title: Memoria y justicia
lessons.grammar: A día de hoy: hablar de la situación actual
lessons.goal: Read how these countries tried, imperfectly and unevenly, to reckon with the past -- Argentina's Punto Final and Obediencia Debida amnesty laws and their annulment, and memory sites like the former ESMA.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 25 Consolidation
lessons.goal: Consolidate repression, censorship, disappearance, resistance and memory.

lessons.title: Nicaragua
lessons.grammar: Una vez que: marcar el punto de partida de algo nuevo
lessons.goal: Read how the Somoza dynasty in Nicaragua was overthrown in 1979 by the Sandinista Front, which then faced the difficult task of governing a country devastated by war.

lessons.title: El Salvador
lessons.grammar: Al cabo de: el tiempo transcurrido
lessons.goal: Read how a twelve-year civil war in El Salvador, intensified by social inequality, left about 75,000 dead, including the army's massacre of civilians at El Mozote.

lessons.title: Guatemala
lessons.grammar: De ahí en adelante: continuar una narración desde un punto
lessons.goal: Read how the internal armed conflict that followed the 1954 coup dragged on for thirty-six years, with violence in the Maya highlands that kept intensifying until the conflict ended in 1996.

lessons.title: Intervención y Guerra Fría
lessons.grammar: A instancias de: señalar quién impulsó una acción
lessons.goal: Read how the Central American conflicts became Cold War proxy wars -- US funding of the Contras, Congress's limit on aid, Cuban and Soviet support, and a UN-backed commission's findings on Guatemala.

lessons.title: Los Acuerdos de Paz
lessons.grammar: No sin antes: reconocer un paso previo necesario
lessons.goal: Read how the Sandinista elections, the 1992 Peace Accords and Guatemala's late peace each ended these wars through negotiation, not military victory -- and what those settlements left unresolved.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 26 Consolidation
lessons.grammar: consolidation of revolution, conflict, intervention and peace
lessons.goal: Consolidate revolution, civil conflict, intervention and peace-building.

lessons.title: Chile
lessons.goal: Read how Pinochet called an October 1988 plebiscite to project legitimacy, and how he stayed on as commander in chief in a transition many considered incomplete -- not the 1973 coup, already covered.

lessons.title: Argentina
lessons.goal: Read about the succession of Argentina's military presidents (Viola, Galtieri, Bignone) and how Galtieri's Falklands invasion preceded the regime's move toward civilian government -- not the coup or the disappearances, already covered.

lessons.title: Uruguay
lessons.goal: Read how Uruguay's regime, after militarily defeating the Tupamaros by 1972, controlled public life through obligatory party affiliation and fear of surveillance, and was surprised when citizens rejected its new constitution.

lessons.title: Operación Cóndor
lessons.goal: Read how the Southern Cone dictatorships built a coordinated network, Operation Condor, to share intelligence and track down exiled dissidents across borders, and how the Terror Archives later documented it.

lessons.title: Democracia y memoria
lessons.goal: Read a closing comparison of how Argentina, Chile, and Uruguay each confronted their dictatorships' legacies differently -- early trials, truth commissions (Rettig, Valech), and Uruguay's distinct pattern.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 27 Consolidation
lessons.grammar: consolidation of dictatorship, repression, coordination, memory and democracy
lessons.goal: Consolidate dictatorship, repression, coordination, memory and democracy.

lessons.title: La deuda crece
lessons.goal: Read how the 1970s oil shocks flooded international banks with petrodollars, which they lent heavily to Latin American governments -- leaving the region dangerously exposed by 1982.

lessons.title: La crisis de 1982
lessons.goal: Read how the US Federal Reserve's interest rate hikes under Volcker made Latin American debt suddenly unpayable, and how the August 1982 payments crisis followed.

lessons.title: Austeridad
lessons.goal: Read how IMF-backed adjustment programs attached conditions -- above all public spending cuts -- to new loans, and the sovereignty debate this sparked across the region.

lessons.title: El coste social
lessons.goal: Read how spending cuts and inflation eroded real wages and fueled the informal sector and rising poverty across the 1980s, including hyperinflation in Bolivia and Peru.

lessons.title: Una década perdida
lessons.goal: Read why the 1980s became known as Latin America's "lost decade" -- near-zero per capita growth, a debt that kept growing anyway, and the Brady Plan that finally marked its formal end.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 28 Consolidation
lessons.grammar: debt, adjustment, social consequences and historical synthesis
lessons.goal: Consolidate the main causes, responses and consequences of the Latin American debt crisis.

lessons.title: Las ideas neoliberales
lessons.goal: Read how the Washington Consensus market-reform prescriptions -- fiscal discipline, trade liberalization, privatization -- were adopted by most 1990s Latin American governments after the debt crisis.

lessons.title: Privatización
lessons.goal: Read how Argentina under Menem and Mexico under Salinas privatized major state enterprises in the 1990s -- and the efficiency arguments for it and the job-loss and pricing controversies against it.

lessons.title: El mercado y el Estado
lessons.goal: Read how 1990s reforms moved away from the statist model toward a market-driven one with lower tariffs, more independent central banks, and active courting of foreign investment.

lessons.title: Desigualdad y pobreza
lessons.goal: Read how 1990s macroeconomic recovery -- lower inflation, renewed growth -- coexisted with persistent or worsening inequality, jobless growth, and Latin America's world-leading Gini coefficients.

lessons.title: El legado neoliberal
lessons.goal: Read a closing, balanced assessment of the neoliberal decade -- the inflation-taming success of the reforms, against the structural fragility exposed by Mexico's 1994 Tequila Effect and the 2001 collapse of Argentina's convertibility.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 29 Consolidation
lessons.grammar: reform, competition, social consequences and historical síntesis
lessons.goal: Consolidate the main causes, responses and consequences of the Latin American neoliberal reforms.

lessons.title: Volver a votar
lessons.goal: Read how, one after another between 1979 and 1990, Latin American countries returned to elected civilian government -- gradually in some cases, after a political crisis in others -- and then faced the debt crisis.

lessons.title: Nuevas instituciones
lessons.goal: Read how new democracies wrote entirely new constitutions -- Brazil's new charter, Colombia's constituent assembly, and Paraguay's new constitution limiting executive power -- plus the region-wide rise of independent electoral tribunals.

lessons.title: Democracia y justicia
lessons.goal: Read how Brazil took a starkly different path from Argentina or Chile -- an amnesty that left victims demanding justice, and a largely disregarded international court ruling that Brazil could not ignore its international obligations.

lessons.title: Las dificultades de la transición
lessons.goal: Read how Serrano's attempted move in Guatemala failed without his army's firm backing, and how crises in Brazil, Ecuador and Argentina were resolved through civil and constitutional channels.

lessons.title: Democracias imperfectas
lessons.goal: Read a closing assessment of these new democracies -- periodic clean elections as the sole undisputed source of legitimacy, presidents governing as if the vote gave them an unlimited mandate, persistent inequality, and limited institutional trust.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 30 Consolidation
lessons.goal: Consolidate language for democratic transitions, institutions, justice, political challenges and evaluation.

lessons.title: Pueblos indígenas
lessons.goal: Read about Latin America's more than forty million Indigenous people across hundreds of distinct peoples and languages, and the near-total lack of official recognition most states gave them for most of the twentieth century.

lessons.title: Tierra y derechos
lessons.goal: Read how the 1989 ILO Convention 169 gave Indigenous movements a key legal tool for land rights, alongside the subsoil-resource conflicts it raised and the term resguardo for an Indigenous reserve.

lessons.title: Identidad y reconocimiento
lessons.goal: Read how constitutions across the region stopped treating themselves as culturally uniform -- Colombia's multiethnic definition, the 1990s reform wave, Ecuador's 1998 and 2008 changes, and Bolivia's 2009 Plurinational State.

lessons.title: Movilización política
lessons.goal: Read three landmark moments of Indigenous political mobilization: Ecuador's 1990 CONAIE uprising, Mexico's January 1994 Zapatista rebellion, and the Bolivian movements around Evo Morales and the Water and Gas Wars.

lessons.title: Nuevas voces
lessons.goal: Read a closing look at the growth of Indigenous political representation, the 2007 UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, and the persistent gaps and resource conflicts alongside these gains.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 31 Consolidation
lessons.goal: Consolidate language for Indigenous identity, land, rights, political mobilisation and contemporary representation.

lessons.title: ¿Por qué integrarse?
lessons.goal: Read how Bolívar's dream of unity, the ALALC (LAFTA), and the 1990s push for new-generation trade treaties after the debt crisis built the case for Latin American regional integration.

lessons.title: Mercosur
lessons.goal: Read how the 1991 Treaty of Asunción created Mercosur among four countries, its trade goals, the 1985 Argentina-Brazil rapprochement behind it, and the dominance of Brazil and Argentina in the bloc's decisions.

lessons.title: Comunidad Andina
lessons.goal: Read how Chile (1976) and later Venezuela left the Andean bloc por su cuenta, alongside the NAFTA treaty negotiated by Salinas de Gortari and its uneven impact on Mexican regions.

lessons.title: Comercio y cooperación
lessons.goal: Read how NAFTA boosted Mexican export manufacturing, the 1994 US proposal for a hemispheric free-trade zone and Chávez's rejection of it, and the region's growing number of overlapping trade agreements.

lessons.title: Una región unida
lessons.goal: Read a closing assessment of Latin American integration -- a fragmented map and lasting institutions, against still-modest intra-regional trade and Bolívar's still-unrealized dream, plus the roads, pipelines and power links meant to unite peoples.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 32 Consolidation
lessons.goal: Consolidate language for regional integration, trade, cooperation, opportunities and limitations.

units.title: The End of the Cold War

lessons.goal: Read how the fall of the Berlin Wall, which dismantled socialism in Eastern Europe, marked a turning point that reached Latin America too, as guerrillas lost their backing and sought negotiated exits.

lessons.title: Un nuevo mundo
lessons.grammar: orden posterior a la Guerra Fría
lessons.goal: Read how the Soviet Union's dissolution ended the bipolar order and produced a "unipolar moment", and how the 1989 US invasion of Panama showed that force remained in play before later debates challenged this interpretation.

lessons.title: Nuevas prioridades
lessons.goal: Read how US policy toward Latin America shifted from a single anti-communist axis to new axes, including free trade through the Enterprise for the Americas Initiative and the fight against drug trafficking in the Andes.

lessons.title: América Latina después de la Guerra Fría
lessons.goal: Read how Cuba, suddenly without Soviet aid and cheap oil, was left with no room to respond to a severe economic crisis that hit its factories and its energy supply.

lessons.title: Hacia los años noventa
lessons.goal: Read a closing synthesis of this unit's storylines -- the end of the Cold War system, Washington's reordered priorities, Cuba's crisis, and the left's reinvention -- and the transformed international framework the region entered the 1990s within.

lessons.label: Review
lessons.title: Unit 33 Consolidation
lessons.goal: Consolidate language for global change, the post-Cold War order, political and economic priorities, regional consequences and transition.

lessons.title: Los años de Menem
lessons.goal: Read about the economic and political side of Menem's Argentina -- Cavallo's convertibility plan, the 1994 constitutional reform enabling his 1995 reelection, the risks of an overvalued currency anchor, and the personal style behind his popularity.

lessons.title: Fujimori y Perú
lessons.goal: Read about Alberto Fujimori's Peru -- the "Fujishock" adjustment program, his initial popularity despite charges of authoritarianism, the 1992 autogolpe, and the capture of Abimael Guzmán.

lessons.title: México y el TLCAN
lessons.grammar: A raíz de que: como consecuencia directa de que (algo ocurriera)
